timeline/deep-time-timeline.summary: The Deep-Time Timeline keeps the long record of Earth before humans: the forming of the planet, the first kindling of life, the slow breathing-in of oxygen, the mass extinctions, and the evolution of the lineage that would lead, at last, to humans.

extra.title: How to Read This
extra.html: Here gather the events and organisms dated before about 300,000 years ago. For the whole sequence, turn to the Master Timeline; for the last 300,000 years, turn to the Human Timeline, where the younger story is kept.

timeline/human-timeline.summary: The Human Timeline keeps the last 300,000 years: the origin of Homo sapiens, the prehistoric dispersals, the early states, the world religions, the empires, and at last the modern era, each age laid down upon the one before like layers of river silt.

extra.title: How to Read This
extra.html: Here gather the events, people, cultures, technologies and places dated from about 300,000 years ago onward. For earlier history, turn to the Deep-Time Timeline; for the combined sequence, to the Master Timeline.

timeline/master-timeline.summary: The Master Timeline sets every era and event in the vault in chronological order, one long procession that runs from the formation of the Solar System to the present.

extra.title: How to Read This
extra.html: Dates are counted in years relative to 1 CE, and a negative year is BCE. Deep-time dates are given in Ga (billions of years ago), Ma (millions) or ka (thousands), the measures of an older clock. All dates before about 1000 CE are approximate, lamps seen through fog.
